full_description: Learn to build practical backend systems using Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL. This hands-on Node.js Backend Development with Express course teaches server-side JavaScript, REST API development, relational database integration, authentication, authorization, testing and backend deployment. Complete a portfolio-ready business operations REST API featuring a PostgreSQL database, authenticated users, protected CRUD operations, authorization tests and a deployable demonstration. This programme emphasizes maintainable code, correct API behavior, database reliability, security fundamentals and working technical evidence.

overview: Node.js Backend Development with Express is an intensive 8-week, 64-hour intermediate certification course engineered to equip developers with production-grade backend engineering competencies. Centered around modern 2027 backend practices, the curriculum establishes rigorous foundations across the Node.js runtime, asynchronous I/O mechanics, Express REST API architecture, and PostgreSQL relational data persistence using parameterized queries and migrations. Students master essential backend security practices—including adaptive password hashing, authentication middleware, role-based access control, and mandatory object-level authorization (preventing OWASP BOLA/IDOR vulnerabilities). best_practices: Mandatory SQL Parameterization: Always pass dynamic values as query parameters ($1, $2); never concatenate untrusted strings into SQL.
Strict Object-Level Authorization: Always verify that the authenticated user owns or has explicit permission to access the requested resource ID.
Never Store Plaintext Passwords: Use adaptive password hashing (Argon2id or bcrypt with high work factor) with unique salt per user.
Generic Authentication Errors: Return generic 'Invalid credentials' messages to prevent user enumeration attacks.
Single Connection for Transactions: Always acquire a dedicated client from the pool for BEGIN, queries, COMMIT, and release it in a finally block.
Never Leak Implementation Details: Centralized error handlers must sanitize responses, hiding stack traces, SQL errors, and internal paths.
Input Schema Validation: Validate headers, query parameters, route params, and request bodies with strict schemas before hitting controllers.
Environment Secrets Hygiene: Keep credentials out of version control, commit only .env.example, and validate process.env on startup.
common_mistakes: Assuming authentication equals authorization: allowing any logged-in user to view or edit any record simply by guessing an ID (BOLA/IDOR).
Using string interpolation to build SQL queries, creating critical SQL injection vulnerabilities.
Using unhandled Promise rejections in async route handlers, causing server hangs or unhandled crashes.
Executing multi-statement transactions across separate pool.query() calls that use different database connections.
Trusting client-supplied ownership fields (e.g. reading owner_id from req.body instead of req.user.id).
Allowing users to elevate their privileges during registration by passing { role: 'admin' } in the request body.
Returning HTTP 200 OK for error responses or using non-standard status codes.
Deploying an Express backend to static web hosts (such as GitHub Pages) and expecting it to execute server-side code.
freelance_applications: Building custom REST APIs and administrative backends for mobile and web applications.
Integrating PostgreSQL databases with Node.js applications for small and medium enterprises.
Refactoring insecure backend codebases to implement authentication, Zod validation, and parameterized SQL.
Creating multi-user booking, scheduling, and business record management services.

testing_requirements: Server Execution: Server boots cleanly in production mode with valid environment configuration and connects to PostgreSQL.
Migration Execution: Database schema migrations apply cleanly from empty database state to current version.
Parameterized Queries: Zero SQL injection vulnerabilities; all dynamic queries utilize $1, $2 parameter placeholders.
Authentication Integrity: Passwords securely hashed with adaptive algorithms; invalid credentials return generic 401 responses.
Cross-User Access Denial: User A cannot read, modify, or delete User B's private records under any circumstance.
Privilege Escalation Denial: Users cannot self-assign administrator roles via request payloads during registration or profile update.
Transaction Rollback: Multi-step transactions execute atomically and roll back completely if any step fails.
Error Sanitization: Internal server errors return structured JSON without leaking database passwords, stack traces, or SQL text.

competency_gates: SQL Safety Gate: Any presence of unsafe SQL string concatenation results in immediate course failure.

BOLA / IDOR Gate: If a user can read, update, or delete another user's private records without authorization, the project cannot pass.
Code Ownership Gate: Students must be able to explain their asynchronous flow, middleware pipeline, and SQL logic; unverified AI-generated code is rejected.

Asynchronous programming with Promises and async/await for non-blocking I/O.
Managing dependencies, npm scripts, and ES modules with package.json.
Working with built-in modules (fs/promises, path, process) and runtime environment variables.
Debugging Node.js applications using VS Code breakpoints and inspector flags.

Multi-statement business workflows: when multiple database operations must succeed or fail together
Critical node-postgres rule: acquiring a single dedicated client for transaction blocks
Executing transactions: BEGIN -> queries -> COMMIT; ROLLBACK in catch block
Ensuring client release in finally blocks to prevent pool exhaustion leaks
Writing automated tests to verify transaction rollback behavior on deliberate failures

modules.hands_on_practice: Replace the in-memory data store in your Express application with PostgreSQL, implementing connection pooling, running schema migrations, querying with parameterized SQL, and building a multi-step transactional business operation with verified rollback on failure.
modules.assignment: Build a PostgreSQL-backed data repository layer with migrations for users and business records, foreign key relationships, parameterized CRUD operations, unique constraint handling, and a transactional multi-step workflow.
modules.business_application: Relational integrity, parameterized queries, and ACID transactions are essential for financial, e-commerce, and enterprise applications where data corruption or injection attacks carry catastrophic legal and business costs.
modules.expected_outcome: Students can connect Express to PostgreSQL, execute safe parameterized SQL, manage migrations, and implement robust multi-statement transactions.
modules.portfolio_contribution: Provides the complete relational database architecture, schema migrations, and persistent data access layer for the capstone API.

modules.title: Authentication & Backend Security
modules.objective: Master user authentication, adaptive password hashing, role-based authorization, mandatory object-level authorization (resource ownership), Zod input validation, and rate limiting.
modules.module_purpose: Equip students with practical backend security engineering skills, moving beyond simple login to enforce strict resource-level access control and protect APIs against OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities.
what_you_will_learn: The critical difference between authentication ('Who are you?') and authorization ('What are you permitted to do?').
Secure password handling with adaptive hashing (Argon2id or bcrypt) and timing-safe verification.
Server-managed session and signed token authentication mechanisms and secure cookie policies.
Building authentication middleware to establish verified identity context (req.user).
Role-based access control (RBAC) and mandatory object-level authorization (resource ownership).
Preventing OWASP Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR) via query scoping.
Validating request bodies, params, and query strings using strict Zod schemas.
Implementing rate limiting on sensitive authentication endpoints to prevent brute-force attacks.

lessons.title: Authentication Fundamentals & Password Security
subtopics: The foundational difference: Authentication (Identity) vs Authorization (Permissions)
User registration and login workflow mechanics
Password security principles: why plaintext, reversible encryption, and MD5/SHA256 are dangerous
Adaptive password hashing with Argon2id or bcrypt: computational cost, memory cost, and unique salts
Timing-safe password verification and returning generic error responses ('Invalid credentials')
Strict policy: never logging passwords, tokens, or credentials in application logs

lessons.title: Session & Token Authentication Architectures
subtopics: Server-managed session architecture: session identifiers, session stores, and lifecycle
Secure browser cookie configuration: HttpOnly (XSS protection), Secure (HTTPS only), SameSite (CSRF mitigation)
Session expiration, session regeneration on login, and clean invalidation on logout
Signed token concepts: signature verification, expiration timestamps, and secret management
Understanding token revocation challenges and comparing sessions vs tokens for business APIs

lessons.title: Authentication Middleware & Identity Context
subtopics: Building reusable authentication middleware to guard protected API routes
Extracting and verifying credentials from sessions or authorization headers
Attaching verified user identity to the request context (req.user = { id, email, role })
Rejecting unauthenticated requests with HTTP 401 Unauthorized
Preventing privilege escalation: ensuring registration endpoints ignore client-submitted role fields

lessons.title: Role-Based & Object-Level Authorization
subtopics: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): restricting endpoints by user role (User, Manager, Admin)
Why RBAC alone is insufficient: introducing Object-Level Authorization (Resource Ownership)
Understanding OWASP #1: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA / IDOR)
Enforcing ownership: verifying the authenticated user owns or has rights to the target record ID
Enforcing ownership in database queries: SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE id = $1 AND owner_id = $2
Preventing mass assignment vulnerabilities: explicitly allowlisting modifiable fields

lessons.title: Request Validation & Rate Limiting
subtopics: Input validation principles: validating all untrusted data before it reaches controllers
Schema definition with Zod: string lengths, email formats, enum values, and positive numbers
Building validation middleware that strips unexpected fields and returns structured 400 errors
Rate limiting with express-rate-limit: configuring limits on login and registration routes
Security headers with Helmet (X-Content-Type-Options, Frameguard, HSTS overview)

modules.hands_on_practice: Build a Secure User Operations & Authorization module in Express featuring user registration with Argon2id/bcrypt hashing, login/logout endpoints, authentication middleware, role checks, object-level ownership verification, Zod input validation, and rate limiting.
modules.assignment: Implement protected CRUD routes where normal users can only read, update, and delete their own business records, managers can access team records, input data is validated with Zod, and brute-force attempts are throttled.
modules.business_application: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) is the #1 vulnerability on the OWASP API Security Top 10; enforcing server-side ownership checks protects sensitive corporate and user data from unauthorized access.
modules.expected_outcome: Students can implement robust authentication, enforce object-level authorization, validate input schemas with Zod, and protect backend endpoints against common security vulnerabilities.
modules.portfolio_contribution: Supplies the core security architecture, authentication middleware, and permission rules protecting all business resources in the capstone.

Configuring the Node.js built-in test runner or equivalent with supertest for HTTP testing.
Setting up dedicated test databases, executing migrations, and managing fixture teardown.
Writing comprehensive integration tests for CRUD endpoints and validation failures.
Mandatory execution of all 10 security acceptance tests (cross-user read/update/delete denial).
Implementing structured JSON logging and unauthenticated health check endpoints (/health).
Authoring clear API documentation using Postman collections and OpenAPI specifications.
key_concepts: Testing HTTP Status Codes & Error Payloads

Testing terminology: unit tests, integration tests, test fixtures, and assertions
Using the Node.js built-in test runner (node:test, node:assert) or equivalent testing tools
HTTP integration testing with supertest: making programmatic requests to Express app instances

lessons.title: API Integration & Endpoint Testing

Automating schema migration execution before running test suites
Writing tests for successful CRUD workflows: create record, fetch by ID, update, and delete
Testing input validation failures: verifying 400 Bad Request and structured error payloads
Database test cleanup: resetting test records between test suites to ensure test isolation

lessons.title: Security & Authorization Test Suites

Testing unauthenticated requests: verifying 401 Unauthorized on protected routes
Testing wrong password and invalid credential handling
Testing cross-user read denial: verifying User A cannot read Record B (403 or 404)
Testing cross-user modification denial: User A cannot update or delete Record B
Testing role elevation denial: verifying regular users cannot access manager endpoints

lessons.title: Structured Logging & Reliability

Log levels: error, warn, info, and debug; setting log levels per environment
Request context in logs: timestamps, HTTP method, URL path, status code, and duration
Sanitizing log output: strictly preventing passwords, tokens, or personal data from appearing in logs
Building an unauthenticated health check endpoint (/health) that confirms server and DB connectivity

Documenting endpoints: method, URL path, authentication requirements, and role permissions
Documenting request schemas, URL parameters, query parameters, and JSON payloads
Documenting response schemas, success status codes, and error response examples
Exporting and organizing complete Postman collections and OpenAPI / Swagger specifications

faq.question: What is Node.js Backend Development with Express?
faq.answer: Node.js Backend Development with Express is an intensive 8-week, 64-hour practical programming certification course that teaches you to build secure, robust server-side applications and REST APIs. You will master the Node.js runtime, asynchronous non-blocking I/O, Express 5 routing and middleware, PostgreSQL relational database integration with parameterized SQL and migrations, user authentication, role-based and object-level authorization, input validation with Zod, automated backend testing, and cloud deployment.

faq.question: Is this course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: This is an intermediate-level course. It is designed for developers who already have working proficiency in JavaScript fundamentals (variables, functions, arrays, objects, ES modules, Promises, and async/await) and basic HTTP concepts. If you are entirely new to programming or JavaScript, we strongly recommend completing Nova Skills Course 56 (Modern JavaScript & TypeScript Foundations) first before taking this backend specialization.

faq.question: What JavaScript knowledge is required?
faq.answer: You should be comfortable with modern JavaScript (ES6+): let and const declarations, arrow functions, object and array destructuring, spread/rest operators, array manipulation methods (map, filter, reduce), ES module syntax (import/export), Promises, and async/await syntax. You should also understand how to produce and parse JSON objects and handle basic runtime errors.

faq.question: What is the duration and fee?
faq.answer: The course spans 8 weeks with 64 guided learning hours (8 hours per week, consisting of 4 hours of interactive lectures and code-alongs plus 4 hours of hands-on software labs). The course fee is a transparent, flat ₹10,900 with zero hidden charges, covering all lectures, software labs, code reviews, and certificate verification.

faq.question: What is the difference between Node.js and browser JavaScript?
faq.answer: While both use the JavaScript language and V8 engine, browser JavaScript runs inside a sandboxed browser environment with access to DOM APIs (window, document) for manipulating user interfaces. Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform runtime environment that executes JavaScript outside the browser on servers, providing access to operating system APIs such as the filesystem (fs), network sockets, environment variables (process.env), and database drivers.

faq.question: What is Express.js?
faq.answer: Express.js is the most popular, minimal, and flexible web application framework for Node.js. It provides a robust suite of features for building web and mobile APIs, including an intuitive routing system, middleware pipelines for processing HTTP requests, controller organization, and standardized error handling.

faq.question: Will I learn REST API development?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn how to design and build professional RESTful APIs adhering to standard HTTP semantics. This includes proper resource naming conventions, using HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) correctly, returning standard HTTP status codes (200, 201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 500), and implementing pagination, sorting, and filtering.

faq.question: What are Express middleware and controllers?
faq.answer: Middleware functions are functions that have access to the request object (req), response object (res), and the next middleware function in the application’s request-response cycle. They perform tasks such as parsing JSON bodies, validating inputs, checking authentication, and logging. Controllers are specialized functions that receive the validated request, execute business logic (often calling database services), and return the final HTTP response.

faq.question: Which database will I learn?
faq.answer: You will learn PostgreSQL, the world's most advanced open-source relational database. You will use the official node-postgres (pg) client library to manage connection pools, execute parameterized queries, implement foreign key relationships, run schema migrations, and manage multi-statement ACID transactions.

faq.question: Why is PostgreSQL the primary database?
faq.answer: PostgreSQL is standardized as the primary database because real-world commercial backend systems overwhelmingly rely on relational data integrity, strict schema constraints, foreign key relationships, and ACID transaction guarantees. Learning relational database modeling and SQL provides essential, transferable backend skills demanded by modern employers.

faq.question: Will I also learn MongoDB?
faq.answer: MongoDB is included as a brief conceptual comparison in Module 03 to contrast relational schemas with document-oriented NoSQL models and discuss their respective trade-offs. However, all core coursework, labs, and the portfolio capstone are standardized on PostgreSQL to ensure deep, production-grade competence rather than surface-level familiarity.

faq.question: Do I need SQL knowledge before joining?
faq.answer: Prior SQL knowledge is helpful but not strictly required. The essential SQL needed to design tables, define foreign keys, write queries, and manage migrations is taught just-in-time during Module 03. For students wanting a comprehensive foundation in advanced database administration and complex querying, Nova Skills Course 59 (Database Foundation) is recommended.

faq.question: Is Course 59 recommended?
faq.answer: Yes. Nova Skills Course 59 (Database Foundation) is recommended as a complementary course for students who want a deep, dedicated foundation in advanced relational database design, complex SQL joins, indexing strategies, and database optimization. However, Course 58 teaches all the SQL necessary to build and deploy your backend capstone.

faq.question: Will I learn CRUD operations?
faq.answer: Yes. You will master full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations using SQL queries executed from Express controllers. You will learn how to fetch collections, retrieve single records by ID, insert new records with RETURNING clauses, update records with dynamic fields, and delete records while respecting foreign key constraints.

faq.question: What are parameterized SQL queries?
faq.answer: Parameterized SQL queries separate the SQL command code from user-supplied data values by using numbered placeholders ($1, $2) rather than concatenating user input directly into SQL strings. The database driver transmits the parameters separately, ensuring that user input can never be interpreted as executable SQL, completely eliminating SQL injection vulnerabilities.

faq.question: Does the course teach database transactions?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn how to manage multi-statement ACID transactions where multiple database updates must either all succeed together or all roll back on error. You will learn how to acquire a single dedicated client connection from the pg.Pool, execute BEGIN, perform queries, execute COMMIT, and ensure ROLLBACK in error handlers with safe client release.

faq.question: Will I learn user authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn how to build complete user authentication systems, including user registration, secure login credential verification, session management with secure cookies (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite), signed token verification, and logout invalidation, along with authentication middleware to protect private API routes.

faq.question: Does the course cover password hashing?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn modern password security practices adhering to OWASP guidelines. You will use adaptive password hashing algorithms (Argon2id or bcrypt with high work factors) that incorporate unique salt per user and computational work factors, making brute-force and rainbow table attacks infeasible. You will also learn why plaintext passwords or fast hashes like MD5/SHA256 must never be used.

faq.question: What is the difference between authentication and authorization?
faq.answer: Authentication verifies identity ('Who are you?'), confirming that a user is who they claim to be through credentials such as email and password. Authorization determines permissions ('What are you allowed to do?'), verifying whether an authenticated user has permission to access, modify, or delete a specific resource or execute an administrative action.

faq.question: Will I learn role-based permissions?
faq.answer: Yes. You will implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) middleware to restrict specific administrative routes or operations to users with designated roles (e.g., User vs Manager vs Admin). You will also learn why public registration endpoints must never permit users to assign themselves elevated roles via request payloads.

faq.question: What is object-level authorization?
faq.answer: Object-level authorization (resource ownership verification) ensures that an authenticated user can only view, edit, or delete records they specifically own or have been granted access to. It prevents Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR)—the #1 API security vulnerability—where an attacker accesses other users' private records simply by changing an ID in the URL.

faq.question: Will I learn secure input validation?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn how to use Zod to define strict validation schemas for request bodies, URL route parameters, and query parameters. Incoming requests that fail schema validation are rejected with structured 400 Bad Request error responses before any business logic or database queries execute, stripping unexpected fields and preventing mass-assignment vulnerabilities.

faq.question: Does the course include rate limiting?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn how to implement rate limiting on public and sensitive endpoints (such as login and registration routes) using middleware like express-rate-limit. Rate limiting restricts the number of requests an IP address can make within a time window, mitigating brute-force password guessing and denial-of-service abuse.

faq.question: Will I learn Postman?
faq.answer: Yes. Postman is used extensively throughout the course for manual API testing, environment variable configuration, automated test scripts, and creating shared request collections. You will export a complete Postman collection documenting all capstone endpoints with example requests and responses.

faq.question: Does the course teach automated backend testing?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn how to write automated integration tests using the Node.js built-in test runner or equivalent frameworks combined with supertest. You will test HTTP status codes, JSON response schemas, validation failures, database persistence, and execute mandatory cross-user security denial tests against an isolated test database.

faq.question: Will I learn API documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn how to produce professional API documentation that specifies endpoint paths, HTTP methods, headers, authentication requirements, role permissions, request JSON schemas, response bodies, and error formats using Postman collections and OpenAPI / Swagger standards.

faq.question: Will I build a complete backend project?
faq.answer: Yes. You will build exactly ONE comprehensive, production-style Business Operations REST API capstone featuring user authentication, role checks, object-level authorization, PostgreSQL persistence, ACID transactions, Zod input validation, automated integration tests, and cloud deployment.

faq.question: What will the business operations capstone include?
faq.answer: The Business Operations REST API capstone includes user registration and login with Argon2id/bcrypt, PostgreSQL database migrations and seed scripts, parameterized CRUD operations for business resources (tasks, projects, or service records), a multi-statement transaction, role and object-level permissions, Zod validation, 10+ passing automated security acceptance tests, and Postman documentation.

faq.question: Will I learn API deployment?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn how to deploy your Express application to a modern cloud hosting platform (such as Render, Railway, or similar platform) and connect it to a hosted PostgreSQL database, managing production environment secrets and verifying health check endpoints.

faq.question: Is GitHub Pages suitable for running Express?
faq.answer: No. GitHub Pages is a static file hosting service designed for client-side HTML, CSS, and client JavaScript. It cannot execute Node.js runtime code, run Express servers, or connect to PostgreSQL databases. We teach deployment using platforms specifically built for server-side Node.js runtimes and database hosting.

faq.question: Does this course cover React frontend development?
faq.answer: No. This course is dedicated exclusively to server-side backend engineering, databases, and API development. If you wish to learn frontend UI development with React, we offer Course 57 (React.js Frontend Development) which seamlessly connects to the APIs built in this course.

faq.question: Does it include advanced cloud architecture?
faq.answer: No. The course focuses on intermediate backend engineering fundamentals (Node runtime, Express, PostgreSQL, authentication, authorization, validation, testing, and deployment). Advanced microservices, Kubernetes, distributed caching clusters, and enterprise multi-region cloud infrastructure are covered in separate advanced programmes.

faq.question: Is it a professional cybersecurity certification?
faq.answer: No. While the course teaches essential secure coding practices (OWASP Top 10 awareness, parameterized SQL, password hashing, and object-level authorization), it is a software engineering certification, not an accredited cybersecurity penetration testing credential.

faq.question: Will I receive source code and API documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. You will build and retain complete ownership of your backend source code repository on GitHub, including all migrations, seed scripts, automated tests, and Postman API documentation, creating a verifiable portfolio artifact to present to employers.

faq.question: What entry-level backend career opportunities are possible?
faq.answer: Graduates are equipped to apply for entry-level and junior backend roles, including Junior Node.js Backend Developer, Express API Developer, Junior Server-Side JavaScript Developer, and Backend Trainee positions, supported by their working GitHub repository and deployed API demonstration.
